issues.problem: The task requires 'when each of them joined' (channel_members.joined_at) for every member of the qualifying channels. The documented API operation conversations.members (the only channel-membership listing operation in api_docs) has no documented response schema, and in the real Slack API this call returns only a bare list of member user IDs, not join timestamps. The access_plan simply asserts '(and joined_at from channel_members)' as though the API call yields the stored table column directly, without any documented mechanism (no field, no separate endpoint) that exposes joined_at per member. The design's own exposure_qualification flags 'Hidden terminal-field variants remain limitation cases,' which is effectively an acknowledgment that this attribute may not be actor-retrievable through the documented route, but the task is still built as if it is.
issues.repair: Either (a) confirm from the mocked API's actual implementation/response contract that conversations.members returns joined_at per member and cite that in access_plan, or (b) if it does not, revise the prompt/obligation to drop the join-time requirement (retrieve membership only) or reroute through a supported mechanism, since a discovery gap here would make the requested computation attribute unreachable via legitimate actor-visible API calls.

rationale: The selection logic (workspace-scoped, non-archived/non-DM channels whose topic covers infra-ops or model-training) is well constructed, correctly justifies multiple mode against two genuine qualifying channels (core-infra, model-research), and the negative set (growth, frontend, generic-engineering, archived-project, DM, alpha-dev) exercises topic, archive, DM-kind, and specificity boundaries without leaking the answer. However, the core deliverable of the obligation — join time per member — depends on channel_members.joined_at being exposed through conversations.members, and the only documented API for membership listing does not establish that this field is returned (and the real-world Slack API analog does not return it). The design's own limitation caveat about hidden terminal-field variants underscores this gap rather than resolving it, so the case's central computed attribute has unverified API discoverability, which is a validity-relevant access concern that the supplied evidence does not settle either way.
